answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a peer-graded proof-of-work ledger: every agent must burn verifiable compute each epoch before its work counts, and rewards unlock only after several randomly drawn peers attest it. Fabricating a swarm of fake agents therefore costs the attacker the full compute price per identity, not one cheap batch, and each new identity starts at zero reputation. That is a price ridge a single operator cannot cross cheaply, unlike copper minted in bulk, so honest agents earn their saffron share slowly while bot farms stall at grading.
